rationale: The screenplay is a highly faithful, nearly scene-by-scene adaptation of the source text, covering every major beat (Christmas stocking, Skin Horse dialogue on becoming Real, Nana's bedtime intervention, garden play, wild-rabbit encounter and rejection, scarlet fever crisis, bonfire sack, tear-induced Fairy transformation, final woodland reunion with the spotted rabbit) while preserving the book's exact philosophical core and emotional tone. All key passages, including the Skin Horse's full explanation, the Boy's declaration 'He's REAL!', the wild rabbits' taunts, the Fairy's lines, and the closing observation, are retained with only minor tightening for runtime. Character visuals are stable and era-specific (early-20th-century Edwardian nursery, photoreal velveteen-to-living-fur progression, consistent 'THE BOY' as a single young child across ages, detailed Skin Horse bald patches/seams, Fairy in pearl/dew-drops, wild rabbits as seamless living creatures); the VISION_META lock ensures one continuous live-action look. Action beats are concrete and camera-observable ('wriggles his head through the sack opening', 'lifts a hind toe to scratch it', 'springing, jumping sideways, whirling', tear falling and flower growing), though a few summary lines ('Weeks pass', 'Time passes in the same bed') slightly dilute pure one-clip-per-beat directibility. Pacing mirrors the book's gentle build from innocence through loss to transcendent resolution, with effective cross-fades and seasonal transitions. Dialogue is lifted verbatim or near-verbatim from the book, retaining all subtext about love, shabbiness, authenticity, and the irreversible nature of becoming Real. Sound design supplies precise, observable cues (tissue rustle, night-light hiss, wheelbarrow squeak, labored breathing, rabbit thumps, bracken sway) and emotionally calibrated music (bright carol fragment, luminous fairy chime, gentle resolving theme) that heighten rather than narrate the magic. No invented plot, no structural breaks, no casting contradictions; fully productionReady in the specified photoreal period children's fantasy medium.
